title: MATLAB Production Server — Logical to Physical Type Mapping (LLM Version)
description: Maps logical schema declarations (x-matlab-* vocabulary, Document 3) to physical schema types (MatlabXxx $defs, Document 2). x-matlab-class is always the literal return value of class() in MATLAB.

general-rules.rule-1: x-matlab-class is the return value of class(x) in MATLAB. For all non-enumeration types this value equals mwtype in the physical encoding.
general-rules.rule-2: x-matlab-shape maps directly to mwsize in the physical encoding. Named free dimensions (e.g. 'N', 'M') are replaced by concrete positive integers at call time. 'scalar' is shorthand for [1,1]. ':' maps to any positive integer value.
general-rules.rule-3: When any dimension in x-matlab-shape is 0, or the array has no elements, the physical encoding is MatlabEmpty regardless of x-matlab-class. struct is excluded — empty struct arrays are not permitted.
general-rules.rule-4: x-matlab-complex:true is only valid for x-matlab-class 'double' or 'single'. All integer classes do not support complex values.
general-rules.rule-5: For enumeration types, class(x) returns the specific enumeration class name (e.g. 'Colors'), not a generic string. This class name becomes mwtype in the physical encoding and is used directly as x-matlab-class in the logical schema.
general-rules.rule-6: x-matlab-fields maps to the keys of mwdata in MatlabStruct. Each field value is a logical type declaration that maps recursively through this table to a physical MatlabValue.
general-rules.rule-7: x-matlab-element-type constrains the type of each element in MatlabCell.mwdata. If absent, elements are unconstrained MatlabValues.
general-rules.rule-8: x-matlab-constraints are semantic constraints applied after type and shape validation. They have no direct physical encoding representation — they are enforced by the server on decoded MATLAB values.

numeric-mapping-rule.description: All numeric classes follow a single parameterized rule. Look up x-matlab-class in the numeric-types table to find the base-type, value range, and physical refs. Then apply the rule below.
numeric-mapping-rule.rule: Given a row in numeric-types with class C: if x-matlab-complex is false, use the real-physical-ref with mwtype C and mwdata containing plain JSON numbers (or NaN/Inf/-Inf for float base-type only). If x-matlab-complex is true and base-type is float, use the complex-physical-ref with mwcomplex:true and mwdata containing [re,im] pairs in column-major order. x-matlab-complex:true is not valid for integer base-type.

numeric-types.precision-note: Full 64-bit precision preserved — not converted to double.
Full 64-bit precision preserved — not converted to double.

non-numeric-mapping.notes: mwdata elements must be JSON true or false only — no numeric 0/1.
mwdata is a single-element JSON array containing one string. For M-by-N char arrays the string contains all M*N characters in column-major order.
MATLAB string array (not char). Each element is a JSON string. Missing values encoded as {"mwdata":"missing"}.
mwdata is a flat column-major array of MatlabValue elements, each independently typed.
mwdata is a JSON object mapping field names to column-major arrays of MatlabValue. Empty struct arrays are not permitted.
TimeStamp values are POSIX milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00 UTC. NaT encodes as NaN. Requires mwmetadata with TimeZone and Format.

x-matlab-class is the specific MATLAB enumeration class name as returned by class() — e.g. 'Colors'. This passes through directly as mwtype. Detected by: class name not present in any other row of this table.

empty-array-override.description: When x-matlab-shape contains a 0 dimension, or the array is otherwise empty, the physical encoding is always MatlabEmpty regardless of x-matlab-class.
empty-array-override.notes: struct is excluded — empty struct arrays are not permitted in MPS JSON encoding.

shape-mapping.description: How x-matlab-shape dimension descriptors map to concrete mwsize values at call time.

rules.notes: Fixed dimension — mwsize value must equal N exactly.
Same letter in multiple positions means equal dimensions. E.g. ['N','N'] = square.
No consistency requirement with other ':' dimensions.
Empty array. Physical encoding is MatlabEmpty. mwsize is always [0,0].

column-major-rule.description: The single most important encoding rule. Applies to all physical array types. MATLAB stores arrays in column-major order — column 1 first, then column 2, and so on. This is the opposite of C and Python/NumPy which use row-major order.
column-major-rule.rule: mwdata is a flat array in column-major order. For an M-by-N array, the element at row r (0-based), column c (0-based) is at mwdata index r + c*M.

example.wrong-reason: Row-major order — this is the C/Python/NumPy convention and is WRONG for MPS encoding

column-major-rule.higher-dimensional: For arrays with more than 2 dimensions, element at indices (i, j, k, ...) (all 0-based) is at mwdata index i + j*dim[0] + k*dim[0]*dim[1] + ... where dim[0], dim[1], ... are the values from mwsize in order.
